identity.title: Disk Evolution Study Through Imaging of Nearby Young Stars (DESTINYS): The SPHERE view of the Orion star-forming region

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present SPHERE/IRDIS H-band data for a sample of 23 stars in the Orion star-forming region observed within the DESTINYS (Disk Evolution Study Through Imaging of Nearby Young Stars) program.
We furthermore used a combination of new and archival ALMA mm-continuum photometry to characterize the dust masses present in the circumstellar disks.

claims.hypothesis: Does scattered light contrast correlate with millimeter flux in the Orion sample?
claims.experiment: Kendall tau test between delta_pol and 1.3 mm flux for detected disks
claims.finding: Correlation exists and arises from the absence of extended, self-shadowed disks in the Orion sample

evidence.quote: This trend is not captured by previous studies of a more diversified sample and is due to the absence of extended, self-shadowed disks in our Orion sample.

claims.hypothesis: Does stellar multiplicity affect disk detection?
claims.experiment: SPHERE total-intensity companion search and Q_phi disk detection in 23 systems
claims.result: 9 systems with companions, 10 with disks, only two disks among the multiple systems
claims.finding: Strong anticorrelation between disk detection and multiplicity

evidence.quote: We find a strong anticorrelation between disk detection and multiplicity, with only two of our ten disk detections located in stellar multiple systems.

claims.hypothesis: Does the external FUV field set the scattered light disk radius?

claims.result: no direct correlation, but no extended disks above ~300 G0
claims.finding: No clear environmental effect on disk radii from FUV in this sample

evidence.quote: While we do not find a direct correlation, we notice that no extended disks are detected above an FUV field strength of $\sim 300$G$_0$.
